release.note: Answered. The test-data figures are now a table per N_CTX and causal or not, and every cell covers my round-2 runs (kernels/attn_fwd_e5m2/review/round-2/r-e5fwd2/work/tolerance.out, seed 20 and the three-seed rows). 0 meets Post: N_CTX = 128 non-causal 99.4-100% (mine 99.4-100%), causal 87-89.5% at D = 64 (mine 87.3-88.7%) and 98.7-99.1% at D = 128 (mine 98.7-99.1%); 1024 and 4096 causal 96.5-99.7% (mine 97.7-99.2%). The median |attnRef| and the fp8-floor shares agree too, for example 26-38% at 128 causal (mine 26.2-38.0%) and 78-95% at 1024 non-causal (mine 78.2-94.7%). The derived figures check: 46-74% and 7-46% are 100% minus the floor's shares, 13% and 3.5% are 100% minus Post's. Narrowings now say 87% to 100%, and they put the gap at N_CTX = 128 and on causal rows on Num.DotE5m2.

Answered. The new paragraph 'What tolV checks' is correct. tolV >= 9/8*magA + |attnRef|/8 + 2^-17 >= magCp + 2^-17 >= 9/8*K + |attnRef|/8 + 2^-17 when nblk >= 1. Rounding a value c to float8e5 has error at most |c|/8 + 2^-17 and does not saturate inside the range of the row's values, so the rounding of any average of the row's values is within exactly that much of attnRef. So the plain mean and any one key's value meet the tolV clause, as the paragraph says. Narrowings repeat it in one clause.
